The **97th Academy Awards** ceremony, presented by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") (AMPAS), took place on March 2, 2025, at the [Dolby Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolby_Theatre "Dolby Theatre") in [Hollywood, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles"). During the gala, the AMPAS presented [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 23 categories honoring [films released in 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film"). The ceremony, televised in the United States by [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") and streamed on [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu"), was produced by Raj Kapoor and Katy Mullan, and was directed by [Hamish Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamish_Hamilton_(director) "Hamish Hamilton (director)").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Hulu-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Production_Team-6) Comedian [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") hosted the show for the first time.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Conan-7)

In related events, the Academy held its 15th [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards") ceremony at the Ray Dolby Ballroom of the [Ovation Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovation_Hollywood "Ovation Hollywood") complex in Hollywood, on November 17, 2024.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Governors_Awards-8) The [Academy Scientific and Technical Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Scientific_and_Technical_Award "Academy Scientific and Technical Award") were presented by host [Diego Luna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Luna "Diego Luna") on April 29, 2025, in a ceremony at the [Academy Museum of Motion Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Museum_of_Motion_Pictures "Academy Museum of Motion Pictures") in Los Angeles.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-9)

*[Anora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anora "Anora")* won a leading five awards, including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Winners-10) Other winners included *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* with three awards; *[Dune: Part Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dune:_Part_Two "Dune: Part Two")*, *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, and *[Wicked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wicked_(2024_film) "Wicked (2024 film)")* with two awards each; and *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")*, *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")*, *[I'm Not a Robot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Not_a_Robot_(film) "I'm Not a Robot (film)")*, *[I'm Still Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film) "I'm Still Here (2024 film)")*, *[In the Shadow of the Cypress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_the_Shadow_of_the_Cypress "In the Shadow of the Cypress")*, *[No Other Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Other_Land "No Other Land")*, *[The Only Girl in the Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Only_Girl_in_the_Orchestra "The Only Girl in the Orchestra")*, *[A Real Pain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Real_Pain "A Real Pain")*, and *[The Substance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Substance "The Substance")* with one each.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Winners-10) The telecast drew 19.69 million viewers in the United States.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Ratings-3)

## Winners and nominees

The nominees for the 97th Academy Awards were announced on January 23, 2025, at the [Samuel Goldwyn Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Goldwyn_Theater "Samuel Goldwyn Theater") in [Beverly Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), by actress [Rachel Sennott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Sennott "Rachel Sennott") and actor [Bowen Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowen_Yang "Bowen Yang").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-11) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* led all nominees with thirteen nominations, the most for a non-English-language film in Oscars history; *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* and *[Wicked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wicked_(2024_film) "Wicked (2024 film)")* tied for second with ten nominations each.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-12) The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 2.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Winners-10)

For the first time in Oscar history, two films, *Emilia Pérez* and *[I'm Still Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film) "I'm Still Here (2024 film)")*, were nominated simultaneously for Best Picture and Best International Feature.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-13) *I'm Still Here* was also the first Portuguese-language film nominated for Best Picture.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-14) With his wins for producing, directing, screenwriting, and film editing *[Anora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anora "Anora")*, [Sean Baker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Baker "Sean Baker") became the second person to win four awards in one night after [Walt Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney "Walt Disney") did so at the [26th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/26th_Academy_Awards "26th Academy Awards") in 1954, and the first to do so for a single film.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-15)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-17) Best Actor winner [Adrien Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Brody "Adrien Brody") gave the longest [acceptance speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_speech "Oscar speech") in Oscar history at 5 minutes and 37 seconds.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-18) Best Actress nominee [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") became the [first openly transgender performer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_LGBTQ_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees#Confirmed_individuals_2 "List of LGBTQ Academy Award winners and nominees") to be nominated for an acting category.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-19) Best Supporting Actress winner [Zoe Saldaña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoe_Saldaña "Zoe Saldaña") was the first [Dominican American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Americans "Dominican Americans") to win an Oscar.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-20) Best Costume Design winner [Paul Tazewell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tazewell "Paul Tazewell") became the first Black man to win that category.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-21) Best Animated Feature winner *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* was the first [independently animated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_animation "Independent animation") film to win that category and the first Latvian film to win an Oscar.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-22) Best Documentary Feature winner *[No Other Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Other_Land "No Other Land")* became the first Palestinian film to win an Oscar.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-23)

## Ceremony information

[![Photo of Conan O'Brien in January 2025.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Conan_O%27Brien_at_the_2025_Sundance_Film_Festival_03_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Conan_O%27Brien_at_the_2025_Sundance_Film_Festival_03_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Conan_O'Brien_at_the_2025_Sundance_Film_Festival_03_(cropped).jpg)[Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien") hosted the 97th Academy Awards.

In October 2024, the Academy hired television producers Raj Kapoor and Katy Mullan to oversee production of the ceremony for the second consecutive year. In a press release, AMPAS president [Janet Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Yang "Janet Yang") and Academy CEO [Bill Kramer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Kramer_(executive) "Bill Kramer (executive)") explained their decision in selecting the pair, stating, "Their love for cinema, their collective creative vision, and their unparalleled expertise in live television make them the perfect team to create an exceptional show for our global audience on the film industry's biggest night." In response, Kapoor and Mullan released a statement, saying, "We are thrilled to lead the brilliant Oscars production team again and work alongside the Academy and [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company "The Walt Disney Company")/[ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABC_News_(United_States) "ABC News (United States)") to help create an unforgettable night of television for movie lovers worldwide."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Production_Team-6) The following month, comedian and former talk show host [Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O'Brien "Conan O'Brien"), who previously hosted two [Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Awards "Primetime Emmy Awards") telecasts in [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_Primetime_Emmy_Awards "54th Primetime Emmy Awards") and [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/58th_Primetime_Emmy_Awards "58th Primetime Emmy Awards"), was selected to host the 2025 gala. "Conan has all the qualities of a great Oscars host — he is incredibly witty, charismatic and funny and has proven himself to be a master of live event television," remarked producers Kapoor and Mullan regarding their choice for host.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Conan-7) Previously, in July, it was reported that comedian and talk show host [Jimmy Kimmel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Kimmel "Jimmy Kimmel"), who had hosted the ceremony four times prior, turned down an invitation to return, while comedian [John Mulaney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Mulaney "John Mulaney") was also allegedly approached and declined.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-34)

The [Southern California wildfires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_2025_Southern_California_wildfires "January 2025 Southern California wildfires") affected the telecast and its surrounding events. Voting for the nominations, which began on January 8, 2025, was originally planned to end four days later. However, due to the wildfires which affected several Academy members, the voting period was extended by five more days ending on January 17. The nominations announcement was also delayed nearly a week to January 23.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-35)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-36) In addition, the annual Academy nominees luncheon originally scheduled for February 10 was cancelled, and the Scientific and Technical Awards gala initially planned for February 18 was delayed by two months to April 29.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-37) At the start of the broadcast, a montage paying tribute to Los Angeles featuring clips from films such as *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")* (2023), *[Everything Everywhere All at Once](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everything_Everywhere_All_at_Once "Everything Everywhere All at Once")* (2022), *[La La Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_La_Land "La La Land")* (2016), *[Mulholland Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mulholland_Drive_(film) "Mulholland Drive (film)")* (2001), and *[The Wizard of Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wizard_of_Oz "The Wizard of Oz")* (1939) was shown prior to [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande")'s performance of "[Over the Rainbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Over_the_Rainbow "Over the Rainbow")".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-38) During the broadcast, a [QR code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code "QR code") was displayed providing a link containing resources for fire relief efforts.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-39) Later, host O'Brien brought onstage a group of twelve firefighters and other first wildfires.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-40)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-41) Three of those members, [Los Angeles Fire For the first time, the broadcast was made available for streaming live on [Hulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu "Hulu").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Hulu-5) The simulcast on said streaming platform was notably met with technical issues such as crashing multiple times throughout the ceremony and prematurely ending the stream just before the Best Actress nominees were announced; Hulu apologized the following day.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-43)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-44)

Notable changes were introduced in the production of the telecast. In a break from previous presentations, the awards for Best Cinematography and Best Costume Design were presented by five actors, one of whom was featured in each of the nominated films in the category.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Empire_Oscars_Live_Blog-28)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-45) The format was similar to how the acting awards were presented at the [81st](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Academy_Awards "81st Academy Awards") and [96th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/96th_Academy_Awards "96th Academy Awards") ceremonies in 2009 and 2024, respectively.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-46) The Academy also announced that none of the five nominees for Best Original Song would be performed live during the gala.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-47) In lieu of the performances, each of the nominated songs was highlighted through personal reflections and behind-the-scenes insight from the creative teams responsible for the nominees.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-48)

Several others participated in the production of the ceremony and related events. Jeff Ross and Mike Sweeney, who previously worked on O'Brien's talk shows, were brought on as co-producers.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-49) Musician [Michael Bearden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bearden "Michael Bearden") was the musical director for the telecast. Production designers Alana Billingsley and Misty Buckley designed a new stage for the show.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Production_Team-6) Comedian and journalist [Amelia Dimoldenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amelia_Dimoldenberg "Amelia Dimoldenberg") served as the social media and red carpet correspondent for the Oscars' online outlets for the second year in a row.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-50) Choreographer [Mandy Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandy_Moore_(choreographer) "Mandy Moore (choreographer)") oversaw the [James Bond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bond "James Bond") musical tribute which featured performances from [Lisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_(rapper) "Lisa (rapper)"), [Doja Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doja_Cat "Doja Cat"), and [Raye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raye "Raye"), and an appearance in the beginning by actress and dancer [Margaret Qualley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Qualley "Margaret Qualley").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-51)

### Best Picture theatrical qualification and other rule changes

In June 2023, the Academy announced that, starting with the 97th awards, all films submitted for Best Picture would have to comply with several standards regarding their theatrical runs.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-RMO-52) In a press release, AMPAS president [Janet Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Yang "Janet Yang") and Academy CEO [Bill Kramer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Kramer_(executive) "Bill Kramer (executive)") said of the new standards, "In support of our mission to celebrate and honor the arts and sciences of moviemaking, it is our hope that this expanded theatrical footprint will increase the visibility of films worldwide and encourage audiences to experience our artform in a theatrical setting. Based on many conversations with industry partners, we feel that this evolution benefits film artists and movie lovers alike."[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-RMO-52) Many media outlets pointed out that the new rules were drafted in response to the growing presence of streaming platforms such as [Amazon Prime Video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video "Amazon Prime Video"), [Apple TV+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_TV_(streaming_service) "Apple TV (streaming service)"), and [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") submitting their films for awards consideration.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-53)

According to the new rules, in addition to the previous requirement where prospective films must play theatrically for a week in either Los Angeles, New York City, Chicago, the San Francisco Bay Area, Atlanta, or Miami,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-55) they also would have to be shown in an expanded seven-day theatrical run in 10 of the top 50 US markets. The expanded theatrical run would have to occur within 45 days after the film's initial release in the eligibility year, and can be shown in either consecutive or nonconsecutive days. For films released later in the calendar year with expansions after January 10, distributors would have to submit to AMPAS release plans for verification and the theatrical run would have to be completed no later than January 24. Non-American films could also have theatrical runs in two markets outside the US to be counted toward ten theatrical markets needed for consideration. However, these films would have to release in the top 15 international theatrical markets in addition to the film's country of origin.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-56)

Additional rule changes were also approved by the AMPAS Board of Governors in April 2024. [Drive-in theaters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drive-in_theater "Drive-in theater"), which were temporarily allowed as a venue to meet qualification and eligibility standards during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), would be no longer recognized as a method to fulfill requirements for consideration.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-57) In the Best Original Score category, up to three composers can receive individual statuettes if all composers contribute significantly to a film's musical score. Additionally, the shortlist for the aforementioned category would increase from fifteen to twenty films. For the screenplay awards, all films must submit a final shooting script to be eligible for consideration in either category. Animated feature films submitted for consideration in the Best International Feature Film category may also be eligible for the Best Animated Feature award provided they meet the rules outlined for both categories. Finally, recipients of the [Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_G._Thalberg_Memorial_Award "Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award") will now receive an Oscar statuette as opposed to a bust of Thalberg in previous years.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Rule_Changes-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-58)

### Box office performance of Best Picture nominees

When the nominations were announced, nine of the ten films nominated for Best Picture had earned a combined gross of $900 million at the American and Canadian box offices at the time.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-CNBC_Oscars-30) *Wicked* was the highest-grossing film among the Best Picture nominees with $466 million in domestic box office receipts. *Dune: Part Two* came in second with $283 million; this was followed by *A Complete Unknown* ($59 million), *Conclave* ($32 million), *The Substance* ($17 million), *Anora* ($15 million), *The Brutalist* ($6 million), *Nickel Boys* ($1.1 million), and *I'm Still Here* ($162,000).[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-59) The box office figures for *Emilia Pérez* were unavailable due to distributor Netflix's policy of refusing to release such figures.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-60)

### Critical reviews

*[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")* chief film critic [Owen Gleiberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Gleiberman "Owen Gleiberman") called the show "a brisk and elegantly executed piece of media stagecraft, successful in more ways than not. It was lavishly designed and purged of dead spots, and the winners were given the chance to reveal who they were, which is really the heart of the show."[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-61) Columnist Brian Lowry of *[TheWrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheWrap "TheWrap")* commented, "The 97th Academy Awards largely mastered the delicate mechanics of that juggling act, acknowledging weightier matters — such as bringing out Los Angeles firefighters for an extended ovation — while seeking to provide a sense of playfulness, even silliness, courtesy of host Conan O'Brien."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-62) Television critic Judy Berman of *[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")* praised O'Brien's hosting performance, writing, "Whenever O'Brien was onstage, balancing impish humor with a palpable love for movies and compassion for an industry where so many recently lost so much to the wildfires that ravaged Los Angeles, the ceremony felt light and loose." She concluded her remarks by stating, "Still, the best moments of this hosting gig were just Conan being Conan, letting the winners enjoy their spotlight and laughing at himself to make everyone else feel comfortable."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-63)

Kelly Lawler of *[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")* reserved praise for O'Brien and the winners' speeches, but she wrote, "Inoffensive and somewhat bland, the 2025 Oscars lacked passion and fervor, or a distinctive hook that makes the ceremony more than just a generic recitation of winners."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-64) Television critic Daniel Fienberg of *[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")* remarked, "I'm perfectly happy to pretend that this telecast was the show we deserved at this point in history, when everything feels so unstable. But maybe it was just an uneven mess. Who's to say?" He criticized several decisions such as dropping the performances of the Best Original Song nominees in favor of musical tributes to James Bond and Quincy Jones that contributed to the telecast's bloated runtime, but he commended O'Brien's hosting performance and called writing during the gala "impressively sharp".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Critic's_Notebook-65) *[The Detroit News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Detroit_News "The Detroit News")* film critic Adam Graham commented, "Sunday night's Academy Awards telecast was severely lacking in the movie star razzle dazzle we look forward to on the broadcast. Coming at the end of a packed awards and entertainment season, it felt more like reheated leftovers than it did Hollywood's biggest night."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-66)

### Ratings and reception

The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 19.69 million people over its length, which was a 1% increase from the previous year's ceremony.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Ratings-3) The show also had 9.1% of households watching the ceremony based on [Nielsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research") estimates, which was lower than the previous ceremony.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-PDF-4) In addition, it garnered a higher 18–49 demo rating with a 4.54 rating among viewers in that demographic. Ratings figures included those who watched the telecast on ABC, streamed it on Hulu, or viewed it on computers, tablets, and other digital devices.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Ratings-3) Its Live+7 rating was 20.283 million people, which made it the 17th highest rated [primetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime "Primetime") telecast in the United States in 2025, behind only sport events.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-67)

In July 2025, the broadcast was nominated for six awards at the [77th Primetime Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/77th_Primetime_Emmy_Awards "77th Primetime Emmy Awards") and its corresponding [Creative Arts Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/77th_Primetime_Creative_Arts_Emmy_Awards "77th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-68) Two months later, the ceremony won one of those nominations for [Outstanding Production Design for a Variety Special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Production_Design_for_a_Variety_Special "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Production Design for a Variety Special") (Production Designers: Alana Billingsley and Misty Buckley; Art Directors: John Zuiker and Margaux LaPresle).[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-69)

***I'm Still Here*** ([Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language"): ***Ainda Estou Aqui*** ; Brazilian Portuguese: [[aˈĩdɐ isˈtow aˈki]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Portuguese "Help:IPA/Portuguese")) is a 2024 [political](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_cinema "Political cinema") [biographical drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film") film directed by [Walter Salles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Salles "Walter Salles") from a screenplay by Murilo Hauser and Heitor Lorega, based on [Marcelo Rubens Paiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcelo_Rubens_Paiva "Marcelo Rubens Paiva")'s 2015 [memoir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ainda_Estou_Aqui "Ainda Estou Aqui") of the same name. It stars [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") and [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro") as [Eunice Paiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eunice_Paiva "Eunice Paiva"), a mother and activist coping with the [forced disappearance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forced_disappearance "Forced disappearance") of her husband, the dissident politician [Rubens Paiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubens_Paiva "Rubens Paiva") ([Selton Mello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selton_Mello "Selton Mello")), during the [military dictatorship in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_dictatorship_in_Brazil "Military dictatorship in Brazil").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-:0-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-5)

The film had its world premiere at the [81st Venice International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Venice_International_Film_Festival "81st Venice International Film Festival") on 1 September 2024,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-:1-6) where it won the [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Film_Festival_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Venice Film Festival Award for Best Screenplay") award and received critical acclaim with widespread praise for Torres' performance.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-Bunbury-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-Tartaglione-8) It was named one of the [Top 5 International Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review:_Top_Five_International_Films "National Board of Review: Top Five International Films") of 2024 by the [National Board of Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review "National Board of Review").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-NBR-9) At the [82nd Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards "82nd Golden Globe Awards"), Torres won the [Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama") award while the film was nominated for [Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film"), a category in which it was also nominated at the [Critics' Choice Movie Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Movie_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "Critics' Choice Movie Award for Best Foreign Language Film") and the [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film_Not_in_the_English_Language "BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language"). At the [97th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards "97th Academy Awards"), the film was nominated for [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") and [Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") (Torres),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-12) and won [Best International Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film"), becoming the first-ever Brazilian-produced film to win an Academy Award.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-13)

Soon after its release in Brazilian theaters on 7 November 2024 by [Sony Pictures Releasing International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Pictures_Releasing_International "Sony Pictures Releasing International"), the film was the target of an unsuccessful boycott by the [Brazilian far-right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolsonarism "Bolsonarism"), which denies that the military regime was a dictatorship.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-14) Grossing $36 million with a budget of around $9M,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-orcado_em_r-2) it became the highest-grossing Brazilian film since the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil "COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-15)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-:5-3)

## Plot

In December 1970, former Brazilian congressman [Rubens Paiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubens_Paiva "Rubens Paiva") lives in a house near [Leblon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leblon "Leblon") beach in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro") with his wife [Eunice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eunice_Paiva "Eunice Paiva") and their five children. Returning to his civil career, after the revocation of his tenure as a congressman following the [1964 Brazilian coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Brazilian_coup_d'état "1964 Brazilian coup d'état"), Paiva continues to support political expatriates without disclosing his activities to his family.

After [revolutionary movements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_struggle_against_the_Brazilian_military_dictatorship "Armed struggle against the Brazilian military dictatorship") kidnap the Swiss ambassador to Brazil, the country faces looming political instability. The Paivas' friends [Fernando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Gasparian?action=edit&redlink=1 "Fernando Gasparian (page does not exist)") [[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando%20Gasparian "pt:Fernando Gasparian")] and Dalva Gasparian decide to seek refuge in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), taking the Paivas' eldest daughter, Vera, with them. Vera had previously witnessed military violence while returning from the cinema with her friends. Paiva's house is raided by the military and he is [arrested and disappears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_people_killed_by_and_disappeared_during_the_Brazilian_military_dictatorship "List of people killed by and disappeared during the Brazilian military dictatorship") in January 1971. Eunice's public inquiries about his whereabouts result in her arrest and torture for 12 days, during which she is questioned about her husband's involvement in pro-democracy movements, which she denies. Eliana, their teenage daughter, is also imprisoned but soon released.

Newspaper reports claim that Rubens fled the country into exile, but Eunice and her friends suspect otherwise. With the help of lawyer Lino Machado, she files a [habeas corpus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habeas_corpus "Habeas corpus") petition. She also learns from family friend Bocaiuva Cunha that Rubens had been secretly helping political exiles. A former teacher, Martha, confirms she was imprisoned with Rubens but is afraid to speak out publicly. She later writes a letter detailing her arrest. Félix, a journalist and family friend, informs Eunice that Rubens was killed, but the military authorities refuse to confirm it. Left to care for her children alone, Eunice sells their home and moves to [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo "São Paulo"), anticipating a new start close to her maternal family.

Twenty five years later, in 1996, surrounded by journalists while receiving Rubens Paiva's official death certificate from the [Brazilian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Brazil_(1985–present) "History of Brazil (1985–present)"), now once again a democracy, Eunice calls for reparations for victims' families and accountability for the military dictatorship's crimes.

In 2014, during a family gathering surrounded by her children and grandchildren, the now 85-year-old Eunice lives with advanced [Alzheimer's disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alzheimer's_disease "Alzheimer's disease"). When a news report about the [National Truth Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Truth_Commission "National Truth Commission") addresses Rubens's case, a distressed Eunice appears to remember him.

An epilogue reveals that five men were identified as responsible for the murder of Paiva, who was killed at the [DOI-CODI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DOI-CODI "DOI-CODI") headquarters between January 21 and 22, 1971, but none were prosecuted. The epilogue also notes that Eunice graduated from law school at 48 and became one of the few experts on [indigenous rights in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_rights_in_Brazil "Indigenous rights in Brazil"), serving as a counselor for the [federal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_Brazil "Federal government of Brazil"), the [World Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank "World Bank"), and the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"). She died in 2018 at the age of 89.

## Production

### Development

The screenplay is by Murilo Hauser and Heitor Lorega. It is adapted from the memoir *[Ainda Estou Aqui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ainda_Estou_Aqui "Ainda Estou Aqui")* by [Marcelo Rubens Paiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcelo_Rubens_Paiva "Marcelo Rubens Paiva"), Eunice's son.

The Brazilian-French co-production was produced by RT Features and VideoFilmes in collaboration with [Globoplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globoplay "Globoplay"), Mact Productions, Conspiração Filmes and [Arte France Cinéma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arte_France_Cinéma "Arte France Cinéma").

### Filming

[Principal photography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_photography "Principal photography") began during May and June 2023 on location in [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), during November and December filming took place in [Sāo Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/São_Paulo "São Paulo"), shooting for 16 weeks in total.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-:7-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-19) Cinematographer Adrian Teijido shot the production on [35mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/35_mm_movie_film "35 mm movie film"), aiming to recreate the Brazilian 1970's mood, selected scenes were also shot in [Super 8mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_8_film "Super 8 film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-:7-17)

## Reception

### Box office

On its opening day in Brazil, *I'm Still Here* brought 50,320 people to the cinemas, grossing [R$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_real "Brazilian real")1.1 million.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-34) In its first weekend, even though it was the target of a frustrated boycott by the [Brazilian far right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolsonarism "Bolsonarism"),[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-:3-35) the film debuted in first place at the box office with 358,000 admissions, earning R$8.6 million, surpassing the third week of *[Venom: The Last Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom:_The_Last_Dance "Venom: The Last Dance")* (R$6.6 million) and fellow new release *[Red One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_One_(film) "Red One (film)")* (R$5.3 million).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-36)

It was released in Portugal on January 16, 2025, where it quickly became popular, surpassing 100,000 spectators within two weeks, according to the Portuguese newspaper *Público*.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-38)

By February 2025, the film had surpassed 5 million admissions in Brazil, becoming the highest-grossing Brazilian film since the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil "COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil"), grossing $25 million during its national theatrical release.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-:6-40)

Alongside international markets, the film grossed a total of $36 million.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-:5-3)

### Critical response

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/ImStillHereBFILFF131024_%284_of_36%29_%2854065967346%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-ImStillHereBFILFF131024_%284_of_36%29_%2854065967346%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ImStillHereBFILFF131024_(4_of_36)_(54065967346)_(cropped).jpg)

[Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") garnered widespread critical acclaim for her performance and earned an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") nomination for [Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress").

Upon its release, *I'm Still Here* received overwhelming praise from the public, film critics, and the press; Torres's performance was particularly acclaimed.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-41) On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 97% of 205 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 8.2/10. The website's consensus reads: "Carried along by Fernanda Torres' superb performance, *I'm Still Here* poignantly explores a nation's upheaval through one family's search for answers."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-42) [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 85 out of 100, based on 43 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-Metacritic-43)

Jessica Kiang of *[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")* praised the film and its dramatic charge: "Classical in form but radical in empathy, *I'm Still Here* arguably does not need the follow-up sections—one set in 1996 and the other in 2014—that somewhat alter the emotional rhythm. But on the other hand, these characters are so vivid that we don't want to leave them either".[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-44) For Wendy Ide of *[Screen Daily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Daily "Screen Daily")*, Salles "never over-labours the film's emotional beats, relying instead on Torres' magnificent, intricately layered performance to drive the picture"; she also praised Montenegro, "who has a brief but exceptionally powerful cameo here as the elderly Eunice".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-45)

Several international outlets applauded Torres's performance, with *[Collider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collider_(website) "Collider (website)")* considering it one of the best of the year and "more than deserving of an [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actress "Academy Award for Best Actress") nomination".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-:4-46) In her review for *[Deadline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")*, Stephanie Bunbury calls the film a "celebration of Brazil" and praises Torres, writing that she "has an emotional delicacy as Eunice that conveys, through the smallest and subtlest signals, what it costs her to hold back her anxiety and anger for the sake of her family. It is a performance that should catapult her into the awards race, 25 years after her mother Fernanda Montenegro was Oscar-nominated for Salles' breakthrough feature, *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")*".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-Bunbury-7) David Rooney in *[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")* highlighted the relationship between Montenegro and Torres, writing, "What makes the connection even more poignant is that she appears as the elderly, infirm version of the protagonist". He called *I'm Still Here* "a gripping, profoundly touching film with a deep well of [pathos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathos "Pathos"). It's one of Salles' best".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-47) For [IndieWire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndieWire "IndieWire"), Leila Latif called Torres's performance "as spectacular as her filmography would suggest, having marked herself out as one of the South American continent's greatest actors in roles in *[Foreign Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Land_(film) "Foreign Land (film)")* (also directed by Salles) and won a [Best Actress Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival_Award_for_Best_Actress "Cannes Film Festival Award for Best Actress") in *[Love Me Forever or Never](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Me_Forever_or_Never "Love Me Forever or Never")*. Her Eunice possesses phenomenal strength and stoicism which make each moment of pain that peep through the chinks of her armor all the more moving". Latif also praised Torres's on-screen interaction with Selton Mello.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-48)

Filmmaker [Alfonso Cuarón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_Cuarón "Alfonso Cuarón") named it one of his favorite films of 2024, saying, "Watching a Walter Salles film is to be embraced in generosity, is like experiencing a gravitational pull, both lifting and grounding us at the same time with an invisible yet undeniable force. With *I'm Still Here*, this effect is even more compelling.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-49) Many other filmmakers, including [Nicole Holofcener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Holofcener "Nicole Holofcener") and [Chad Hartigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Hartigan "Chad Hartigan"), also cited it as among their favorite films of 2024.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-50)

In 2025, *[Collider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collider_(website) "Collider (website)")* ranked it third on its list of the "10 Essential Movies of the 2020s So Far", with Eddie Possehl writing, "With the disease of misinformation and government corruption spreading across the real world, the story told within *I'm Still Here* is a vital watch for people of every age as society continues to evolve and degrade at the same time."[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-51)

*I'm Still Here* was named one of the [Top 5 International Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review:_Top_Five_International_Films "National Board of Review: Top Five International Films") of 2024 by the [National Board of Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review "National Board of Review")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-NBR-9) and one of 50 Best Films of the year by British film magazine *[Sight & Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sight_and_Sound "Sight and Sound")*.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-52) In July 2025, it ranked 253rd in the "Readers' Choice" edition of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*'s list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-53)

At the [82nd Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards "82nd Golden Globe Awards"), the film received two nominations: [Best Foreign Language Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Foreign_Language_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film") and [Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama") for Torres. Torres won in her category, becoming the first Brazilian actress to win a [Golden Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards") in an acting category.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-54) The film was also nominated for [Best Film Not in the English Language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Film_Not_in_the_English_Language "BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language") at the [78th British Academy Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/78th_British_Academy_Film_Awards "78th British Academy Film Awards").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-55)

At the [97th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards "97th Academy Awards"), the film received three nominations, including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"), becoming the first time a Brazilian film was nominated in the category.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-56) It won the award for [Best International Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_International_Feature_Film "Academy Award for Best International Feature Film") (the first Brazilian film to win after four nominations).[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-57) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* was considered a front-runner, but controversies around [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") and an attempt to smear *I'm Still Here*'s campaign led most pundits to agree it ceased France's chances to win the category after more than thirty years.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-60)

On 17 February 2025, the film received [Cinema for Peace Dove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_for_Peace_awards "Cinema for Peace awards") for the Most Valuable Film of the Year.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-61) Shortly after, at the [12th Platino Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12th_Platino_Awards "12th Platino Awards") held in Madrid on 27 April 2025, it won Best Ibero-American Fiction Film, Best Director for Walter Salles, and Best Actress for Fernanda Torres.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-62)

### Cultural impact

Brazilians widely embraced *I'm Still Here*, as its release coincided with the celebrations marking 40 years since the restoration of democracy in Brazil[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-63), and because country still pays reparations for the regime's victims families, following an amnesty approved during the Military dictatorship that prevented accountability for crimes committed by the regime officials.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-64)

The film's success resonated during the 2025 [Brazilian Carnival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Carnival "Brazilian Carnival") season: Torres was a prominent figure in the festivities. Shops reported a surge in demand for costumes inspired by her Golden Globes outfit, and stores along the [Rua 25 de Março](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rua_25_de_Março "Rua 25 de Março")" in São Paulo were filled with Oscar statue props and costumes.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Still_Here_(2024_film)#cite_note-66)

***The Brutalist*** is a 2024 [epic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_film "Epic film") [period drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_drama "Historical drama") film directed and produced by [Brady Corbet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brady_Corbet "Brady Corbet"), who co-wrote the screenplay with [Mona Fastvold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mona_Fastvold "Mona Fastvold"). It stars [Adrien Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Brody "Adrien Brody") as a [Jewish-Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Hungary "History of the Jews in Hungary") architect and severely traumatized [Holocaust survivor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Holocaust_in_Hungary "The Holocaust in Hungary") who emigrates to the United States, where he struggles to recover and get his life back on track. The cast also features [Felicity Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felicity_Jones "Felicity Jones"), [Guy Pearce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Pearce "Guy Pearce"), [Joe Alwyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Alwyn "Joe Alwyn"), [Raffey Cassidy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffey_Cassidy "Raffey Cassidy"), [Stacy Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stacy_Martin "Stacy Martin"), [Emma Laird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Laird "Emma Laird"), [Isaach de Bankolé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaach_de_Bankolé "Isaach de Bankolé"), and [Alessandro Nivola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Nivola "Alessandro Nivola"). The film was shot using the [VistaVision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VistaVision "VistaVision") format which had been originally developed in the 1950s, and was the first film shot in the format since *[One-Eyed Jacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-Eyed_Jacks "One-Eyed Jacks")* in 1961.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-7)

A co-production of the United States, the United Kingdom, and Hungary, *The Brutalist* premiered at the [81st Venice International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Venice_International_Film_Festival "81st Venice International Film Festival") on September 1, 2024, where Corbet was awarded the [Silver Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Lion "Silver Lion") for Best Direction. It was released in the United States by [A24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A24 "A24") on December 20, 2024; in Hungary by [UIP-DunaFilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_International_Pictures "United International Pictures") on January 23, 2025; and in the United Kingdom and Latin America by [Focus Features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_Features "Focus Features") through [Universal Pictures International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures#Units "Universal Pictures") on January 24, 2025.

The film received critical acclaim and grossed $50.4 million against a $9.6 million budget. Among [multiple accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_received_by_The_Brutalist "List of accolades received by The Brutalist"), the film earned ten nominations at the [97th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards "97th Academy Awards"), including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture"), winning for [Best Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Cinematography "Academy Award for Best Cinematography"), [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Academy Award for Best Original Score"), and [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor") for Brody. At the [82nd Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards "82nd Golden Globe Awards"), it won three awards, including [Best Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Drama"). It was named one of the top ten films of 2024 by the [American Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute "American Film Institute").

## Plot

### Overture

Hungarian-Jewish [Holocaust survivor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocaust_survivor "Holocaust survivor") and [Bauhaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bauhaus "Bauhaus")-trained architect László Tóth arrives in the United States after being forcibly separated from his wife, Erzsébet, and orphaned niece, Zsófia. As his ship enters [New York Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Harbor "New York Harbor"), he sees the [Statue of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty "Statue of Liberty").

### Part 1: The Enigma of Arrival

In 1947, László travels to [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia") and stays with his cousin, Attila. He discovers that Attila has [assimilated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish_assimilation "Jewish assimilation"), anglicizing his name and converting to Catholicism. Attila reveals to a relieved László that Erzsébet and Zsófia are still alive but stuck in Europe. He offers László work with his furniture business, and the two are soon approached by Harry Lee Van Buren, who wishes to surprise his father, wealthy industrialist Harrison Lee Van Buren, with a renovated library at his mansion near [Doylestown, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doylestown,_Pennsylvania "Doylestown, Pennsylvania"). Following a drunken night of merriment where Attila and his wife Audrey both encourage László to dance with her, Audrey expresses her disdain for László and suggests he live elsewhere. Back at the mansion, Harrison is enraged by the surprise renovation and fires the men; Harry refuses to pay them. Attila blames László for the failed project, falsely accuses him of having made a pass at Audrey, and demands that he leave their home.

Three years later, László, now a [heroin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroin "Heroin") addict, works as a laborer loading coal and lives in [charity housing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeless_shelter "Homeless shelter") with his friend Gordon, an African-American single father. Harrison turns up to tell him the architectural community has lauded his modern library renovation, and that he has discovered László's past as an accomplished architect in Europe. He pays the money owed and invites László to a party, where he commissions a grand project in tribute to his late mother: The Van Buren Institute, a community center comprising a library, theater, gymnasium, and chapel. Work begins immediately with László living on site and employing Gordon. Harrison introduces László to his personal lawyer, who expedites the immigration of László's wife and niece.

### Part 2: The Hard Core of Beauty

In 1953, Erzsébet and Zsófia reunite with László in Philadelphia and he discovers that as a result of their [wartime suffering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Budapest "Siege of Budapest"), Erzsébet is a full-time wheelchair user due to [osteoporosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteoporosis "Osteoporosis"), and Zsófia is [unable to speak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_mutism "Selective mutism"). During construction, László clashes with contractors and consultants hired by Harrison, who depart from his design in an attempt to stay on budget. He agrees to work unpaid to make up for additional costs. Harry derides László as being merely "tolerated" and makes lewd remarks about Zsófia. Following the derailment of a train carrying materials and ensuing legal costs, a furious Harrison abandons the project and fires the workers.

In 1958, László and Erzsébet have moved to New York City, where he works as a draftsman at an architecture firm, and she writes for a newspaper. Zsófia, having recovered her ability to speak, is expecting a child with her husband, Binyamin. They announce they are [making Aliyah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliyah "Aliyah") and moving to [Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem"), much to the chagrin of László and Erzsébet. Harrison restarts the project and rehires László.

While visiting [Carrara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrara "Carrara") to purchase [marble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrara_marble "Carrara marble"), Harrison rapes an intoxicated László, calling him a societal leech whose people invite their own persecution. László begins to unravel, becoming more belligerent and impulsively firing Gordon during an argument back on site. Recalling the prior contempt he received, he laments to Erzsébet that they are not welcome in America. After László almost kills Erzsébet by giving her heroin to soothe her pain, she proposes they move to Jerusalem and live with Zsófia, to which he agrees. Shortly afterwards, Erzsébet confronts Harrison at his home and calls him a rapist in front of his family and associates. An enraged Harry violently drags her out, before his sister Maggie intervenes and helps her leave. Unable to find his father, Harry organizes a search party and tries to locate him within the institute.

### Epilogue: The First Architecture Biennale

In 1980, Erzsébet has died, and a [retrospective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retrospective "Retrospective") of László's work is held at the first [Venice Biennale of Architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Biennale_of_Architecture "Venice Biennale of Architecture"). The exhibition showcases various projects built around the world in the ensuing years and includes the Van Buren Institute, finally completed in 1973. Zsófia, accompanied by her young adult daughter and an aging, incapacitated László in a wheelchair, gives a revelatory speech asserting that László designed spaces in the structure to resemble both [Buchenwald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buchenwald_concentration_camp "Buchenwald concentration camp") and [Dachau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dachau_concentration_camp "Dachau concentration camp") concentration camps. The structure, she implies, functions as a way of processing trauma. Zsófia ends her speech with a phrase she claims László used to tell her as a struggling young mother: "No matter what the others try and sell you, it is the destination, not the journey."
