## Production

### Development

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Brady_Corbet_at_Berlinale_2024.jpg/250px-Brady_Corbet_at_Berlinale_2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brady_Corbet_at_Berlinale_2024.jpg)Writer/Director [Brady Corbet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brady_Corbet "Brady Corbet") in 2024

In September 2018, *[Deadline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")* reported that director [Brady Corbet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brady_Corbet "Brady Corbet") had chosen the period drama *The Brutalist* as his next project following the world premiere of his second feature film, *[Vox Lux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox_Lux "Vox Lux")* (2018).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline60918-8) New York-based Andrew Lauren Productions (ALP) developed the screenplay with Corbet and financed the film.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline60918-8) Corbet co-wrote the screenplay with his partner [Mona Fastvold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mona_Fastvold "Mona Fastvold"), with whom he co-wrote the psychological drama *[The Childhood of a Leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Childhood_of_a_Leader_(film) "The Childhood of a Leader (film)")* (2015) and the musical film *Vox Lux* (2018).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-variety-9)

The film was originally announced as a co-production between Andrew Lauren and [D.J. Gugenheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D.J._Gugenheim "D.J. Gugenheim") for ALP and Brian Young for Three Six Zero[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline60918-8) and later joined by Trevor Matthews and Nick Gordon for [Brookstreet Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brookstreet_Pictures "Brookstreet Pictures"),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline20920-10) Andrew Morrison of Yellow Bear, the Polish company Madants,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-thr-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-12) and executive produced by [Christine Vachon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Vachon "Christine Vachon"), [Pamela Koffler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pamela_Koffler "Pamela Koffler"), and [David Hinojosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hinojosa "David Hinojosa") of [Killer Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killer_Films "Killer Films").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline20920-10)

On September 2, 2020, *Deadline* announced that [Joel Edgerton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Edgerton "Joel Edgerton") and [Marion Cotillard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_Cotillard "Marion Cotillard") had been cast as the film's leads, László Tóth and Erzsébet Tóth, respectively, and that [Mark Rylance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Rylance "Mark Rylance") was cast in the role of László's mysterious client.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline20920-10) [Sebastian Stan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Stan "Sebastian Stan"), [Vanessa Kirby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Kirby "Vanessa Kirby"), [Isaach De Bankolé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaach_De_Bankolé "Isaach De Bankolé"), [Alessandro Nivola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alessandro_Nivola "Alessandro Nivola"), [Raffey Cassidy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raffey_Cassidy "Raffey Cassidy"), and [Stacy Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stacy_Martin "Stacy Martin") were also announced in unknown roles.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline20920-10) Corbet described *The Brutalist* as "a film which celebrates the triumphs of the most daring and accomplished visionaries; our ancestors", and the project which is so far the closest to his heart and family history.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline20920-10) Protagonist Pictures presented the project to buyers at the [2020 Toronto International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Toronto_International_Film_Festival "2020 Toronto International Film Festival").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline20920-10) The film takes place in Pennsylvania and was shot in four languages: English, Hebrew, Hungarian, and Italian.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-variety-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline20920-10)

Director of photography [Lol Crawley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lol_Crawley "Lol Crawley"), editor Dávid Jancsó, and costume designer Kate Forbes were announced on March 9, 2023.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-lux-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-14) Production designer [Judy Becker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Becker "Judy Becker") was announced on April 11, 2023.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline110423-15) [Daniel Blumberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Blumberg "Daniel Blumberg") composed the film's score.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-16)

On April 11, 2023, it was announced that [Adrien Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Brody "Adrien Brody"), [Felicity Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felicity_Jones "Felicity Jones"), [Guy Pearce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Pearce "Guy Pearce"), [Joe Alwyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Alwyn "Joe Alwyn"), [Jonathan Hyde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Hyde "Jonathan Hyde"), [Emma Laird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Laird "Emma Laird"), and [Peter Polycarpou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Polycarpou "Peter Polycarpou") would star in the film, while Edgerton, Cotillard, Rylance, Stan, and Kirby were no longer attached.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline110423-15) It was also announced that the film would be co-produced by the US-based companies Andrew Lauren Productions and Yellow Bear along with the United Kingdom's Brookstreet and Intake Films, and Hungary's Proton Cinema,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline110423-15) and financed by Brookstreet UK, Yellow Bear, Lip Sync Productions, Richmond Pictures, Meyohas Studio, Carte Blanche, Cofiloisirs, and Parable Media.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline110423-15) CAA Media Finance handles US sales with Protagonist Pictures handling international sales.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline110423-15) [Focus Features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_Features "Focus Features") subsequently acquired international distribution rights to the film.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-focus-4)

Corbet dedicated the film to [Scott Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Walker_(singer) "Scott Walker (singer)"), who had died in 2019, and who had scored his previous films.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-17)

### Writing

Corbet had long had an interest in architecture. His uncle is an architect who studied at [Taliesin West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliesin_West "Taliesin West"), which Corbet frequented as a child, while Fastvold's grandfather was a mid-century designer.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-script011425-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-austinchronicle-19) Corbet stated that the film is about the parallels between the artistic experience and the immigrant experience, and that [brutalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brutalist_architecture "Brutalist architecture"), in addition to its highly cinematic nature, would work as the perfect visual allegory for exploring post-war trauma.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-script011425-18)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-thr090924-20) Fastvold's own experience as an immigrant from Norway also informed the writing of the film.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-script011425-18) Furthermore, Corbet considered architecture and filmmaking to be similar processes, as they are both "forms of artistic expression that require an extraordinary amount of participation from other people, collaboration and lots of money".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-script011425-18)

The character of László Tóth was inspired by several real-life architects and designers, including [Marcel Breuer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcel_Breuer "Marcel Breuer"), [Paul Rudolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Rudolph_(architect) "Paul Rudolph (architect)"), [Ludwig Mies van der Rohe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_Mies_van_der_Rohe "Ludwig Mies van der Rohe"), [László Moholy-Nagy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/László_Moholy-Nagy "László Moholy-Nagy"), [Louis Kahn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Kahn "Louis Kahn"),[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-thr090924-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-range-21) and [Ernő Goldfinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernő_Goldfinger "Ernő Goldfinger").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-22) During their research, Corbet and Fastvold consulted architectural historian [Jean-Louis Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Louis_Cohen "Jean-Louis Cohen") (who died in 2023); Cohen noted that no actual examples of architects that emerged from the war with a career like Tóth's in fact existed.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-nyt122324-23) Alongside Cohen's *Architecture in Uniform: Designing and Building for the Second World War*, Hilary Thimmesh's *Marcel Breuer and a Committee of Twelve Plan a Church: A Monastic Memoir*, a book chronicling the construction of [Saint John's Abbey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_John's_Abbey,_Collegeville "Saint John's Abbey, Collegeville") in [Collegeville, Minnesota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collegeville,_Minnesota "Collegeville, Minnesota") by the Hungary-born, Bauhaus-trained Breuer, was an additional point of reference.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-nyt122324-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-bbc-24) Corbet further cited the writings of [W. G. Sebald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W._G._Sebald "W. G. Sebald") and [V. S. Naipaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._S._Naipaul "V. S. Naipaul") (whose novel *[The Enigma of Arrival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Enigma_of_Arrival "The Enigma of Arrival")* lends its name to the first part of the film) as influences.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-thr090924-20)

### Filming

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/41/Lol_Crawley_-_IFFR_2025_%28003%29.jpg/250px-Lol_Crawley_-_IFFR_2025_%28003%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lol_Crawley_-_IFFR_2025_(003).jpg)Cinematographer Lol Crawley discussing *The Brutalist* at the [2025 IFFR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_International_Film_Festival_Rotterdam "54th International Film Festival Rotterdam")

Corbet shot the film's epilogue in [Venice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice "Venice") in September 2020. Principal photography, scheduled to start in Poland in December, was postponed due to [COVID](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") restrictions.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-screendaily-25) Further delays occurred as a result of the [war in Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_war_(2022–present) "Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)") as well as several pregnancies (including that of lead actress Felicity Jones) and deaths in the families of the film's cast and crew.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-screendaily-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-gq122324-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-syncreport-27) Corbet ultimately elected to shoot in Hungary to take advantage of its tax credits, the presence of multiple film laboratories in [Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest "Budapest"), as well as his own familiarity; both Corbet and Fastvold had prior experience filming in the country.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-gq122324-26)

Principal photography eventually began on March 16, 2023, in Budapest.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-deadline110423-15)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-29) The Hungarian capital and surrounding countryside doubled as 1950s Philadelphia and rural Pennsylvania in the film, while the [Andrássy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrássy "Andrássy") Castle in [Tóalmás](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tóalmás "Tóalmás") stood in for the Van Buren mansion.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-screendaily-25)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-cntraveler-30) Production then moved to [Carrara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrara "Carrara"), Tuscany, on April 29, 2023.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-32) Filming took place in the Bettogli and Bombarda quarries in unexpected thick fog, and in the town of Carrara itself.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-cntraveler-30) A small camera unit filmed exteriors in New York City, as well as the [Statue of Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statue_of_Liberty "Statue of Liberty") reveal featured in the opening scene.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-kodak-33) Principal photography wrapped after 34 days on May 5, 2023.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-34)

The film was shot using the [VistaVision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VistaVision "VistaVision") process and cameras equipped with Leica-S lenses. It involves shooting horizontally on [35 mm film stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/35_mm_movie_film "35 mm movie film"), which was then scanned, with the intention of also making prints for a [70 mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/70mm_film "70mm film") release, which has the same height and was the most practical format to show the original size of the VistaVision frame when projecting film.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-kodak-33) The idea for VistaVision arose while Corbet and director of photography [Lol Crawley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lol_Crawley "Lol Crawley") were scouting the quarries in Italy. The format was originally intended for big vistas, but ultimately the vast majority of the film was shot on VistaVision.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-kodak-33) Corbet explained that "the best way to access [the 1950s] was to shoot on something that was engineered in that same decade",[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-variety072524-35) while Crawley stated that the format, with its wider field of view, allowed filmmakers to photograph architecture without using distorting wide-angle lenses.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-variety121224-36) Crawley also used [Arricam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arricam "Arricam") ST, LT and [Arriflex 235](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arriflex_235 "Arriflex 235") 35 mm cameras equipped with [Cooke lenses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooke_Optics "Cooke Optics") for the shoot. An [Arriflex 416](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arriflex_416 "Arriflex 416") 16 mm camera equipped with Zeiss Superspeed lenses was used to shoot documentary-style footage, while the TV footage in the epilogue was filmed using a [Digital Betacam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betacam#Digital_Betacam "Betacam").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-kodak-33)

The Van Buren Institute, which was only constructed in portions and as a scale model, was designed by production designer [Judy Becker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judy_Becker "Judy Becker") based on the notes of Fastvold and Corbet, who tried to be as descriptive as they could about its features in the script.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-nyt122324-23) Not an architect by training, Becker looked to the designs of concentration camps, real-life brutalist buildings, the work of Marcel Breuer and [Tadao Ando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tadao_Ando "Tadao Ando"), Louis Kahn's [Salk Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salk_Institute_for_Biological_Studies "Salk Institute for Biological Studies"), [Frank Lloyd Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Lloyd_Wright "Frank Lloyd Wright")'s [Johnson Wax Headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Wax_Headquarters "Johnson Wax Headquarters") and [James Turrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Turrell "James Turrell")'s [skyspaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyspace "Skyspace") for inspiration.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-elledecor-37) She also cited Breuer's Westchester Reform Temple in [Scarsdale, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarsdale,_New_York "Scarsdale, New York"), a synagogue she remembered from her childhood and which had a Star of David overhead, as a point of reference.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-nyt122324-23)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-indiewire010825-38)

### Music

Main article: [The Brutalist (soundtrack)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(soundtrack) "The Brutalist (soundtrack)")

The film's [score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score") was composed by English musician [Daniel Blumberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Blumberg "Daniel Blumberg"), who had previously worked with Corbet on the short film *Gyuto* (2019). The two worked together on the film over a span of seven years.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-shares-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-sensory-40) The album containing the score was released through [Milan Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan_Records "Milan Records") on December 13, 2024.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-sensory-40) Blumberg and Corbet wanted continuous music for the film's first 10 minutes, resulting in the opening sequence of *The Brutalist* being choreographed and shot to Blumberg's [demos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demo_(music) "Demo (music)").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-shares-39) The [overture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overture "Overture") features pianists [John Tilbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Tilbury "John Tilbury"), [Sophie Agnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Agnel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sophie Agnel (page does not exist)") [[fr](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie%20Agnel "fr:Sophie Agnel")], and Simon Sieger, trumpeter [Axel Dörner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axel_Dörner "Axel Dörner"), and saxophonist [Evan Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evan_Parker "Evan Parker"), all of whom appear throughout the soundtrack.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-shares-39) Synth-pop musician [Vince Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Clarke "Vince Clarke") plays the synthesizer on "Epilogue (Venice)".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-sensory-40)

The [experimental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experimental_music "Experimental music") "Construction" was the first track Blumberg wrote for the score; an early demo was composed on a [prepared piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prepared_piano "Prepared piano") at London's [Cafe Oto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cafe_Oto "Cafe Oto") to create a sound similar to construction noises.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-sensory-40) "Erzsébet", one of the score's [themes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theme_(music) "Theme (music)"), was played by Blumberg live on a piano since Corbet wanted the actors to [hear the music while shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diegetic_music "Diegetic music"); the [train noises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Train_noise "Train noise") from the scene were eventually incorporated into the track's final version.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-sensory-40)

### Post-production and A.I. controversy

Editing was completed by Hungarian editor Dávid Jancsó.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-41) In an interview with *RedShark News*, Jancsó revealed that [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") (A.I.) tools from [Respeecher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respeecher "Respeecher"), a Ukrainian software company, were deployed in order to improve the authenticity of Adrien Brody and Felicity Jones's Hungarian dialogue.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-VarietyAI-42) Both actors received [dialect coaching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialect_coach "Dialect coach"), but had troubles with [Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_language "Hungarian language") [phonemes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoneme "Phoneme") since the language is known to be particularly difficult [to learn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_acquisition "Language acquisition") for native English-speakers.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-43) The filmmakers wanted to perfect their pronunciation "so that not even locals will spot any difference."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-VarietyAI-42) Unsuccessful [ADR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubbing#ADR/post-sync "Dubbing") work prompted them to record Brody and Jones's voices into Respeecher; Jancsó, a native Hungarian speaker, also fed in his voice to "finesse the tricky dialect".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-VarietyAI-42)

Director Brady Corbet issued the following statement to *[Deadline Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")* after Jancsó's interview sparked backlash on social media:[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-DeadlineAI-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-:0-45)
> [Brody] and [Jones]'s performances are completely their own. They worked for months with dialect coach Tanera Marshall to perfect their accents. Innovative Respeecher technology was used in Hungarian language dialogue editing only, specifically to refine certain vowels and letters for accuracy. No English language was changed. This was a manual process, done by our sound team and Respeecher in [post-production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-production "Post-production"). The aim was to preserve the authenticity of [Brody] and [Jones]'s performances in another language, not to replace or alter them and done with the utmost respect for the craft.

Before settling on AI as a tool, production considered using auto-tune on ADR, a popular technique in Hollywood.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-47) Dávid Jancsó affirms:[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-:0-45)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-VarietyAI-42)
> There's nothing in the film using AI that hasn't been done before. It just makes the process a lot faster.

Additionally, it was said that [generative artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence "Generative artificial intelligence") was used to conjure a series of architectural blueprints and finished buildings in the film's closing sequence.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-VarietyAI-42) In a 2022 *[Filmmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmmaker_(magazine) "Filmmaker (magazine)")* article, production designer Judy Becker claimed the film's architecture consultant used [Midjourney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midjourney "Midjourney") "to create three brutalist buildings quite quickly."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-48) However, Corbet denied this in a subsequent interview: "Judy Becker and her team did not use AI to create or render any of the buildings. All images were hand-drawn by artists. To clarify, in the memorial video featured in the background of a shot, our editorial team created pictures intentionally designed to look like poor digital renderings circa 1980."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-49) The director concluded by saying "*The Brutalist* is a film about human complexity, and every aspect of its creation was driven by human effort, creativity, and collaboration. We are incredibly proud of our team and what they've accomplished here."[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-DeadlineAI-44)

## Release

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Brady_Corbet_Venice.jpg/250px-Brady_Corbet_Venice.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Brady_Corbet_Venice.jpg)Director Brady Corbet receiving the ARCA Cinema Giovani Award at the [2024 Venice Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Venice_Film_Festival "2024 Venice Film Festival")

*The Brutalist* had its world premiere at the [81st Venice International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Venice_International_Film_Festival "81st Venice International Film Festival") on September 1, 2024, where it competed for the [Golden Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Lion "Golden Lion") and won the [Silver Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Lion "Silver Lion") for Corbet.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-50) It also played at the [Toronto International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Toronto_International_Film_Festival "2024 Toronto International Film Festival") on September 6, 2024.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-51) The film's festival run also included selections for screenings at the [2024 New York Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_New_York_Film_Festival "2024 New York Film Festival"), the [69th Valladolid International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/69th_Valladolid_International_Film_Festival "69th Valladolid International Film Festival"), and the [31st Austin Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Film_Festival "Austin Film Festival").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-54) It was featured in the Limelight section of the [54th International Film Festival Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_International_Film_Festival_Rotterdam "54th International Film Festival Rotterdam") to be screened in February 2025.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-55)

A week after its premiere at Venice, [A24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A24 "A24") acquired U.S. distribution rights to the film for $10–15 million in what was described as a competitive situation.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-57) One distributor that bid for the film was [Neon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neon_(company) "Neon (company)"), although the company's CEO Tom Quinn said that he and Corbet disagreed on whether to delay the film's release to 2025 in order to produce more 70mm prints.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-58) It was released in the U.S. by A24 on December 20, 2024,[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-59) and was released in the United Kingdom and Latin America by [Focus Features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Focus_Features "Focus Features") through [Universal Pictures International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Pictures#Units "Universal Pictures") on January 24, 2025.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-60) In Canada, it was distributed by [Elevation Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevation_Pictures "Elevation Pictures").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-61) It was screened in [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") theaters two days prior to its limited theatrical release for New York and Los Angeles before being screened in IMAX nationwide throughout January.

## Reception

### Box office

*The Brutalist* grossed $16.3 million in the United States and Canada, and $34.1 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $50.4 million.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-numbers-6)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-mojo-3)

*The Brutalist* made $266,791 from four theaters in the US in its opening weekend, and then $211,164 in its second weekend and $244,341 in its third.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-62) In its fourth weekend, the film expanded to 68 theaters and made $1.38 million. Its figure was noted as outperforming *[Better Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Better_Man_(film) "Better Man (film)")*, which made $1.1 million from 1,291 theaters over the same frame.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-64) The following weekend it grossed $2 million from 338 theaters (and a total of $2.4 million over the four-day [MLK holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr._Day "Martin Luther King Jr. Day")).[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-65) After earning 10 Oscar nominations, the film expanded to 1,118 theaters, and made $2.9 million over the weekend.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-66)

### Critical response

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 93% of 337 critics' reviews are positive. The website's consensus reads: "Structurally beautiful and suffused with Adrien Brody's soulful performance, writer-director Brady Corbet's immaculately designed *The Brutalist* is a towering tribute to the immigrant experience."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-67) [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean"), assigned the film a score of 90 out of 100, based on 57 critics, indicating "universal acclaim".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-Metacritic-68)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Adrien_Brody-61584.jpg/250px-Adrien_Brody-61584.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adrien_Brody-61584.jpg)

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Daniel_Blumberg_at_82nd_Venice_International_Film_Festival-1_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Daniel_Blumberg_at_82nd_Venice_International_Film_Festival-1_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Daniel_Blumberg_at_82nd_Venice_International_Film_Festival-1_(cropped).jpg)

[Adrien Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrien_Brody "Adrien Brody") won his second [Academy Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor") for his performance, while [Daniel Blumberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Blumberg "Daniel Blumberg") won the [Academy Award for Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Academy Award for Best Original Score").

*[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")*'s [Peter Bradshaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Bradshaw "Peter Bradshaw") gave the film five out of five stars, calling it "an amazing and engrossing epic". He continued: "*The Brutalist* obviously takes something from [Ayn Rand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayn_Rand "Ayn Rand"), but also from [Bernard Malamud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Malamud "Bernard Malamud") and [Saul Bellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saul_Bellow "Saul Bellow") in its depiction of the US immigrant adventure and the promise of success – but maybe Corbet and Fastvold go further and faster into how dizzyingly sensual and sexual it all is". Bradshaw concluded: "It is an electrifying piece of work, stunningly shot by cinematographer Lol Crawley and superbly designed by Judy Becker. I emerged from this movie light-headed and euphoric, dizzy with rubbernecking at its monumental vastness."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-The_Guardian_2024-09-05-69) [Owen Gleiberman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Gleiberman "Owen Gleiberman") of *[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")* wrote that the film is "paced with a pleasing stateliness" despite its long runtime, and "overflows with incident and emotion (...) as if Corbet were making a biopic about a real person." He favorably compared Brody's work in *The Brutalist* to the actor's Academy Award-winning prior role as an Holocaust survivor in *[The Pianist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pianist_(2002_film) "The Pianist (2002 film)")* (2002), writing that "his performance, even at its quietest, is suffused with tumultuous feeling." He also highly praised Pearce's performance, writing, "Pearce is often a riveting character actor, but it's been a long time since he popped in a role the way he does here. In thick wavy hair and a mustache, speaking with a booming stentorian bluster that's plummy and irresistible, he's like [Clark Gable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_Gable "Clark Gable") playing [Charles Foster Kane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Foster_Kane "Charles Foster Kane")."[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-70)

Brian Tallerico of *[RogerEbert.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RogerEbert.com "RogerEbert.com")* gave *The Brutalist* four out of four stars, describing it as "a film that turns inward into itself, winding its themes around its characters like a great American novel." He called Brody's performance "the best work of his career" and felt Pearce "balances him perfectly" in his portrayal of "a wealthy monster who discards anyone around him once he's used them up," while finding Jones "a bit miscast". He also called the film "a technical marvel" and praised its cinematography, editing, and score.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-71) David Sims of *[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")* interpreted the film as Corbet's "grand canvas to explore his own frustrations with the limits that commerce places on the arts", positively comparing it to the director's previous feature, *[Vox Lux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox_Lux "Vox Lux")* (2018). He wrote: "*Vox Lux* was a film that had me crying out 'I get it!' in frustration; with *The Brutalist*, I said the same line with more satisfaction." Sims called Brody's performance "pained and lived-in" and Pearce's "an excellent performance of a preening cartoon character". Though, he described the second half of the film as "something of a slog" and "unrelenting in its despair", but felt it "plays both better and worse on a second viewing, because the blatant contours of the plot are less jarring."[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-72)

*[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")*'s [Richard Brody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Brody "Richard Brody") was more critical of the film, writing, "Brady Corbet's epic takes on weighty themes, but fails to infuse its characters with the stuff of life."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-73)

The film's use of [VistaVision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VistaVision "VistaVision") led to a revival of industry interest in the format,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-74) with [Paul Thomas Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Thomas_Anderson "Paul Thomas Anderson") using it to film his 2025 film *[One Battle After Another](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Battle_After_Another "One Battle After Another")*,[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-75) as well as [Yorgos Lanthimos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorgos_Lanthimos "Yorgos Lanthimos")'s *[Bugonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugonia_(film) "Bugonia (film)")* (2025), [Alejandro González Iñárritu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alejandro_González_Iñárritu "Alejandro González Iñárritu")'s *[Digger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digger_(2026_film) "Digger (2026 film)")* (2026), [Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig")'s *[Narnia: The Magician's Nephew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narnia:_The_Magician's_Nephew "Narnia: The Magician's Nephew")*, and [M. Night Shyamalan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._Night_Shyamalan "M. Night Shyamalan")'s *[Remain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remain_(film) "Remain (film)")* (both 2027).[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-78)

### Accolades

Main article: [List of accolades received by *The Brutalist*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_accolades_received_by_The_Brutalist "List of accolades received by The Brutalist")

Upon its premiere at the [81st Venice International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Venice_International_Film_Festival "81st Venice International Film Festival"), *The Brutalist* won five awards, including the [Silver Lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Lion "Silver Lion").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-80) It was subsequently nominated for nine awards at the [30th Critics' Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/30th_Critics'_Choice_Awards "30th Critics' Choice Awards"),[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-Critics_Choice-81) ten awards at the [97th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/97th_Academy_Awards "97th Academy Awards") including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-82) It ultimately won three of these, which were [Best Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Cinematography "Academy Award for Best Cinematography"), [Best Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Academy Award for Best Original Score"), and [Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Actor "Academy Award for Best Actor"). It had seven nominations at the [82nd Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards "82nd Golden Globe Awards"), winning three for [Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama"), [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director") and [Best Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Drama").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-guardiangoldenglobes-84) In addition, the [American Film Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute "American Film Institute") named *The Brutalist* as one of the [top 10 films of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Film_Institute_Awards#2024 "American Film Institute Awards").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-AFI-85)

[NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR") included the film in their list of the best movies and TV of 2024, with critic [Bob Mondello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Mondello "Bob Mondello") writing that *The Brutalist* is: "Gorgeous, conceptually stunning, and dizzying in its savagery about cracks in the foundation of the American dream."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-86)

[RogerEbert.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RogerEbert.com "RogerEbert.com") writers named *The Brutalist* to the top slot of the site's Ten Best Films of 2024, which is determined by [Borda count](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borda_count "Borda count") of the site's writers.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-87)

Filmmakers [Tim Fehlbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Fehlbaum "Tim Fehlbaum"), [Drew Goddard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drew_Goddard "Drew Goddard"), [Reinaldo Marcus Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinaldo_Marcus_Green "Reinaldo Marcus Green"), [Don Hertzfeldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Hertzfeldt "Don Hertzfeldt"), [Matt Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Johnson_(director) "Matt Johnson (director)"), [Karyn Kusama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karyn_Kusama "Karyn Kusama"), [David Lowery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lowery_(director) "David Lowery (director)"), [Lance Oppenheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Oppenheim "Lance Oppenheim"), [Paul Schrader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Schrader "Paul Schrader"), [Celine Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celine_Song "Celine Song"), [Oliver Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Stone "Oliver Stone"), [Denis Villeneuve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Villeneuve "Denis Villeneuve"), [Malcolm Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malcolm_Washington "Malcolm Washington"), [John Waters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Waters "John Waters") and [Shea Whigham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shea_Whigham "Shea Whigham") have cited it as among their favorite films of 2024.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-93)

In December 2024, *The Brutalist* topped *[Collider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collider_(website) "Collider (website)")*'s list of the "10 Best Drama Movies of the Last 25 Years", with Liam Gaughan writing: "Brady Corbet crafted a deeply thought-provoking story about the collapse of the American dream, the inescapable greed of capitalism, and the aggressive anti-Semitism that is still pertinent today ... *The Brutalist* is an unforgettable film, and serves as a reminder that true innovations within the industry are still possible."[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-94)

In January 2025, *Coachella Valley Independent* named it "One of the Best Films of the 21st Century", with Bob Grimm writing: "You'll realize you are seeing genius and historic filmmaking in progress — a sprawling, majestic, 3 1/2-hour epic in which every frame is well-played."[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-best-95)

*[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_(website) "Vulture (website)")* also included it on its list of "The Best Movies Over 3 Hours Long", calling it: "A film as colossal as the building at its heart."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-long-96)

In April 2025, *Urban List* included it on its list of "14 of The Best Cinematography Movies Ever Made".[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-movies-97)

In June 2025, *[IndieWire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndieWire "IndieWire")* ranked the film at number 76 on its list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 2020s (So Far)."[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-Best-98)

In July 2025, it was one of the films voted for the "Readers' Choice" edition of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*' list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century," finishing at number 241.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist_(film)#cite_note-99)

# Relatório: Atores Indicados ao 81º e 82º Golden Globes

## Introdução

Este relatório apresenta um panorama completo dos atores indicados tanto ao **81º Golden Globe Awards** (realizado em 7 de janeiro de 2024, premiando produções de 2023) quanto ao **82º Golden Globe Awards** (realizado em 5 de janeiro de 2025, premiando produções de 2024). Os dados foram extraídos das listas oficiais de indicações divulgadas pela Golden Globes.

---

## 1. 81º Golden Globe Awards (2024)

### Filmes – Principais Atores Indicados

| Categoria | Ator(a) | Filme | Função |

## Conclusão

Ambas as cerimônias refletiram a diversidade crescente do cinema e da televisão contemporânea, com destaque para produções independentes, representatividade e inovação. O 82º Golden Globe destacou-se por quebrar recordes históricos, como a indicação de uma atriz trans e a vitória de uma produção não-inglesa, enquanto o 81º celebrou o retorno dos grandes filmes de estúdio tradicional.

The **81st Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony for [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_film "2023 in film") and [American television productions of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_American_television "2023 in American television"). It was broadcast live on January 7, 2024, from [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), beginning at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"), on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") in the United States. It was produced by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions"), [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner"), and [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss"); the latter also served as director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) This was the first ceremony after Dick Clark Productions and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries") took full control of the Golden Globes from the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) The ceremony was also the first to air live on CBS in the United States since [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_Golden_Globe_Awards "39th Golden Globe Awards").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) Comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") hosted the ceremony.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)

The nominees were announced on December 11, 2023. *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")* and *[Succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succession_(TV_series) "Succession (TV series)")* both tied for the most nominations with nine each, followed by *[Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppenheimer_(film) "Oppenheimer (film)")*'s eight.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

The ceremony also featured the debut of two new categories: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)

Additionally, the cultural phenomenon of "[Barbenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbenheimer "Barbenheimer")" received seventeen nominations, winning seven.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15)

## Ceremony information

This was the first Golden Globe Awards ceremony after the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association") (HFPA) disbanded in 2023. On June 12, 2023, the HFPA announced that all of its rights and properties related to the Golden Globes were acquired by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions") and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

On February 21, 2023, the date of the ceremony was announced. It came back on a Sunday night slot after being moved to Tuesday for the previous year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4) On September 18, 2023, [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") were announced as its executive producers and showrunners.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5) On November 17, 2023, it was announced that [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") had acquired the broadcast rights to the ceremony, replacing the Golden Globes' long-time U.S. broadcast partner [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)

The nominations were announced on December 11, 2023, during an event co-hosted by [Cedric the Entertainer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer "Cedric the Entertainer") and [Wilmer Valderrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmer_Valderrama "Wilmer Valderrama"). Most of the categories were revealed during a live-streaming presentation, while ten of the categories were revealed during another segment on *[CBS Mornings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Mornings "CBS Mornings")*.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-18)

On December 21, comedian and actor [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") was announced as the host.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-22) Before this announcement, it was reported that a source with knowledge of the conversations told [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN") that at least five A-list comedic actors, including [Chris Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock "Chris Rock") and [Ali Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Wong "Ali Wong"), declined offers to host; the hosts of the podcast *[SmartLess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SmartLess "SmartLess")* (actors [Will Arnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Arnett "Will Arnett"), [Jason Bateman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bateman "Jason Bateman"), and [Sean Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hayes "Sean Hayes")) also reportedly declined the offer.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-23) That same month, *[TheWrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheWrap "TheWrap")* reported that 64 voters threatened to withhold their final-round votes in protest, after being told that they would not be given tickets to the ceremony.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-24)

With the awards no longer being overseen by the HFPA, a new, racially and ethnically diverse group of voters consisting of 300 journalists representing 76 countries selected the 2023 nominees and winners.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)

For her portrayal of [Mollie Burkhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollie_Kyle "Mollie Kyle") in *[Killers of the Flower Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killers_of_the_Flower_Moon "Killers of the Flower Moon")*, [Lily Gladstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Gladstone "Lily Gladstone") became the first [Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") actor to win a Golden Globe Award, winning for [Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-25)

### Expansion

On September 26, 2023, it was announced that two new categories would be added for the upcoming ceremony: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" (a category for films that grossed at least $100 million domestically and $150 million worldwide) and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")" (also known as "Best Stand-Up Comedian on Television").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-29) Some critics felt that the new categories were an attempt to improve the ceremony's viewership and relevance, with comparisons drawn to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#Proposed_"Popular_Film"_category "91st Academy Awards") to introduce a [category for "Popular Film"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Popular_Film "Academy Award for Outstanding Achievement in Popular Film") in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards "91st Academy Awards").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-33)

### Reduction

The two Lifetime Achievement Awards (the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") and the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award")) were not presented this year, but expected to return in the future. Executive Vice President Tim Gray explained that with the change in ownership and status, and 25 of the competitive categories expanding from 5 nominees to 6, the increase will also include a reduction with no presentation of the two aforementioned awards for this year. "This is not a permanent change, with future awards slated to be given," Gray wrote in a post on the Globes' official website.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-34)

## Reception

### Criticism of Jo Koy's opening monologue

| External videos | |
| --- | --- |
| [![video icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg) [Jo Koy Opening Monologue \| 81st Annual Golden Globes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KvSHHnucouo) | |
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)[Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy"), host of the 81st Golden Globe Awards

Host [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy")'s opening [monologue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monologue "Monologue") was met with criticism from viewers and critics with many describing his jokes as "cringeworthy", "painful", and "unfunny". Chelsey Sanchez of *[Harper's Bazaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harper's_Bazaar "Harper's Bazaar")* described the monologue as "awkward" and "distasteful".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-35) Koy was also criticized for putting blame on his writers during the monologue, coming after the lengthy [2023 Writers Guild of America strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2023 Writers Guild of America strike"). Justin Curto of *[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_(website) "Vulture (website)")* noted that when some of his jokes fell flat, Koy "immediately threw his writers under the bus... He yelled. 'Yo, shut up. You're kidding me, right. Slow down. I wrote some of these and they're the ones you're laughing at'".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-36) Marlow Stern of *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* noted that many of Koy's jokes drew "groans" and "boos" from the audience.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-37)

Among jokes that drew the most ire were those about the film *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")*, and attending nominees [Robert De Niro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_De_Niro "Robert De Niro"), [Meryl Streep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meryl_Streep "Meryl Streep") and [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"); the latter's reaction went viral.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-40) Shirley Li of *[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")* wrote: "Practically every joke failed to land, mostly because the punchlines were dated or obvious."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-41) Nicole Sperling of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*, who was in the audience that night, wrote that she had "never seen an audience rebel against an emcee so quickly" and cited a prominent film director describing the monologue as a "disaster".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-42)

Conversely, four-time [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") host and comedian [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") defended Koy on *[The View](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View "The View")*, saying: "These hosting gigs are brutal. They're just brutal. If you don't know the room, if you've not been in these rooms before and you're sort of thrust out there, it's hit or miss. Now, I love Jo Koy, he makes me crazy because he's funny. I don't know whether it was the room, I don't know whether it was the jokes, I didn't get to see it. But I do know, that he is as good as it gets when it comes to stand-ups and it is not an easy gig."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-43) Actor and comedian [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin") also threw his support behind Koy on [Threads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threads_(social_network) "Threads (social network)"), writing: "I tip my hat to anyone who steps out on stage to host a live awards show. It's a very difficult job and not for the squeamish. I know because I'm still throwing up from the last time I did it in 2010. So, Congratulations to Jo Koy, who took on the toughest gig in show business, hit, missed, was light on his feet, and now has twenty minutes of new material for his stand up!"[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-44)

Additionally, comedian [Michael Che](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Che "Michael Che") supported Koy by writing that "comedians should boycott hosting award shows" on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-45) When questioned about Koy's jokes aimed toward her film *Barbie*, director [Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig") replied that she was not offended.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-46) On *[Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watch_What_Happens_Live_with_Andy_Cohen "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen")*, actor and comedian [Kevin Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Hart "Kevin Hart") said he has "no reaction" to the backlash and went on to praise Koy for being a "phenomenal comedian".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-47) In a [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") post by Filipino actor and comedian [Michael V.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_V. "Michael V."), he posted: "I think Jo Koy's Golden Globes jokes are funny, direct, and pretty much self-explanatory. The last thing Jo Koy should be doing is trying to explain it to people who purposely choose NOT to understand and appreciate them."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-48)

Koy responded to the criticism in an interview with *[Good Morning America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Morning_America "Good Morning America")*, admitting: "I'd be lying if [I said] it doesn't hurt," but also admitted, "I had fun. You know, it was a moment that I'll always remember. Hosting is just a tough gig. Yes, I'm a stand-up comic, but that hosting position it's a different style. I kind of went in and did the writer's thing. We had ten days to write this monologue. It was a crash course. I feel bad, but I got to still say I loved what I did."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-49) In his first stand-up set afterward, Koy mocked the Hollywood celebrities, alluding: "Lot a marshmallows, man. They're delicious, but goddamn, they're soft. I just come from a different time. I see the changes that are happening. I get it, but goddamn, can we fucking laugh at ourselves?"[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-50)

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_(song) "El Mal (song)")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19)
